- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast decline, it often overcorrects; cap peak forecast at 2–3% above recent high.
- In low sentiment (≤0.4) periods, model frequently underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.
- Model tends to lag in early periods (first 3–5 days of forecast) — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows alternating high-low cycles, model often misjudges direction; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; apply linear decay correction: reduce forecast by 0.2–0.5% per day after day 10.
